political_conclusion: NONE — no recommendation to abolish IIT or property tax

who_depends.iit: State general revenue appropriations (largest GR category); education PSF is heavily GR-funded and thus IIT/sales/corporate dependent
who_depends.urt: Traditional school district foundation funding (M&O) under constitutional 25-mill URT
who_depends.school_additional: Local school M&O above foundation and/or debt service
who_depends.county: County general, roads, libraries, hospitals, colleges, other
who_depends.municipal: City general, pensions, libraries, bonds, parks, other

can_plausibly_matter_with_caveats: Corporate/enterprise taxation — partial (~14% of IIT gross at current collections) but already funding GR; not free capacity
Consumption — only family with IIT-scale yield, but naive rate hike is an explicit regressive household burden shift

state_iit_gap.illusion_note: Summing existing corporate+gaming+franchise+severance is NOT incremental capacity — those dollars already fund GR.

regressivity_surface.rule: If a proposed replacement merely shifts burden onto ordinary households through higher prices or regressive consumption taxes, surface that explicitly.
findings: Sales/use is already $3.667B — nearly IIT-scale. Using higher sales rates to retire IIT is a burden rename unless household protections are proven.
Gaming and some consumption excises lean regressive.
Property-tax retirement that dumps cost into local sales options can recreate the same household burden locally.
